picks.rationale: Playground deliberately dropped a working randomizer and hand-authored 1,000 NPCs — a concrete production trade-off between generated volume and authored meaning.
picks.excerpt: Game director Ralph Fulton said that it would save a lot of time, but randomly created NPCs "just didn't make as much sense."
picks.title: Fable Devs Hand-Crafted 1,000 NPCs Instead of Using a Randomizer Tool

picks.rationale: Saber's dev chief lays out where genAI actually sits in his pipeline alongside offshoring and IP strategy — studio-level production economics, not slogans.
picks.excerpt: "Sometimes I play these games and I can just see the wasted money"
picks.title: Saber Interactive's Tim Willits on generative AI, moving development out of North America, and embracing recognisable IP

picks.rationale: CD Projekt's joint-CEO draws a hard line for a flagship RPG: AI as helper tool only, because complex games break under it — a policy other studios will be measured against.
picks.excerpt: AI is a tool that can help, but not for the kinds of "complex" games that CD Projekt makes, its joint-CEO says.
picks.title: The Witcher 4 Will Be Made "Predominantly Using People" And Not AI

picks.rationale: A shipped AI-translation-plus-human-review localisation pipeline on a major license — the practical shape of AI in production, and the backlash it draws.
picks.excerpt: Yu-Gi-Oh Tag Force GX was translated into different languages using AI, with the work being checked over by a human.
picks.title: Yu-Gi-Oh Tag Force GX Is The Latest Game Under Fire Over AI

picks.rationale: A veteran Nintendo art director posts an AI-assisted prototype and gets buried — the clearest test yet of whether AI is tolerated even at the sketching stage.
picks.excerpt: Takaya Imamura was surprised that he was 'getting slammed this hard' for sharing a prototype made with the help of AI
picks.title: Zelda Art Director Receives Backlash For AI Prototype Test
